title: Pair Encoding Preserves Well-Formedness
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $r$ be a finite bit string, and let $C$ be a Boolean circuit with $2n+2+|r|$ inputs, gates in topological order, and a valid output vertex. Suppose every gate has distinct input vertices, every NOT gate has exactly one input, and every gate has at most two inputs. Then the circuit obtained by wiring its inputs to the pair encoding of an $n$-bit input and $r$ has distinct input vertices at each gate, and every NOT gate has exactly one input.
hypotheses_covered: $C$ has gates in topological order with each gate reading only earlier vertices
Every gate of $C$ has distinct input vertices
Every NOT gate of $C$ has exactly one input
Every gate of $C$ has at most two inputs
